edges.effect_quant: Prospective cohort data suggest a clinically meaningful but not extreme effect, especially in higher-risk or more exposed groups.
edges.mechanism: Alcohol near bedtime initially enhances GABAergic sedation but later fragments sleep as blood alcohol falls, sympathetic tone rises, and REM rebound occurs. That pattern is especially relevant to REM sleep because the exposure changes sleep architecture rather than just sleep duration.
edges.summary: Prospective cohort data link evening alcohol intake to more disrupted REM sleep in general adult. The average effect is usually moderate rather than dramatic, so this edge is better read as a risk modifier than a stand-alone cause or cure.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.

evidence.notes: Effects of emerging alcohol use on developmental trajectories of functional sleep measures in adolescents.
